claims.section: review body: guard cell sugar sensing and stomatal closure
claims.verbatim_text:
It has further been suggested that sugars themselves do not act as
guard cell osmolytes but are instead degraded by invertase and sucrose synthase producing hexose
monomers that are sensed by hexokinase, and result in stomatal closure via a mechanism mediated
by abscisic acid (ABA) produced in the guard cells (66,89).
claims.claim_statement: Hexose monomers released from sucrose cleavage are sensed by hexokinase and cause stomatal closure through an ABA-mediated mechanism in guard cells, rather than acting as osmolytes.

scope.compartment: guard cell symplast (hexokinase and ABA production inside the guard cell)

claims.section: review body: guard cell sugar sensing and stomatal closure
claims.verbatim_text:

claims.subject: constitutive hexokinase overexpression (enhanced hexose sensing)

claims.claim_statement: Guard-cell hexokinase overexpression accelerated sugar-induced stomatal closure, supporting photosynthesis feedback inhibition of stomatal conductance by sucrose.

scope.species: not stated in span (Kelly et al. 2013 worked in tomato and Arabidopsis)
scope.timescale: not stated in span; framed as photosynthesis feedback

claims.section: Role for Suc Other Than Osmoregulation
claims.verbatim_text:
When the
production of Suc in the mesophyll exceeds phloem
loading, the excess Suc is carried to the guard cells and
stimulates stomatal closure via hexokinase, thereby
reducing water loss when photosynthesis is saturated
(Kelly et al., 2013). Although this process may provide
long-term coordination between transpiration and
photosynthesis, such a mechanism could not account
for short-term coordination between photosynthesis
and stomatal behavior, as reduced stomatal conduc-
tance is not usually observed under conditions of high
photosynthetic rates (Wong et al., 1979; Lawson et al.,
2010, 2014).
claims.claim_statement: Sucrose in excess of phloem loading reaches guard cells and stimulates hexokinase-mediated closure, but this can only provide long-term, not short-term, coordination because reduced conductance is not usually seen at high photosynthetic rates.
claims.subject: excess mesophyll sucrose delivered to guard cells
claims.relation: stimulates closure only on a long timescale, not short-term

scope.compartment: mesophyll-to-guard-cell apoplastic route; hexokinase in guard cell
scope.timescale: explicitly long-term coordination; explicitly NOT short-term

claims.why: It puts an explicit timescale boundary on sugar-driven closure, which is load-bearing because the hypothesis asserts an effect on a single morning after one cold night.

claims.section: review body, end of section V (immediately preceding 'VI. Challenges and perspectives')
claims.verbatim_text:
By contrast, in periods of high A, the excess of sucrose
derived from mesophyll cells would induce stomatal closure by two
mechanisms; via an osmotic effect at the apoplast (Lu et al., 1995,
1997; Kang et al., 2007) and by activating the ABA signalling
pathway within guard cells via hexokinase (Kelly et al., 2013).
claims.claim_statement: During periods of high assimilation, excess mesophyll-derived sucrose is proposed to close stomata by two distinct mechanisms: an osmotic effect in the apoplast and hexokinase-dependent activation of ABA signalling inside the guard cell.
claims.subject: excess mesophyll-derived sucrose during high assimilation
claims.relation: induces closure via an apoplastic osmotic route and a symplastic hexokinase/ABA route

scope.species: not stated in span (cited work in Vicia faba, tomato, Arabidopsis)
scope.compartment: explicitly two compartments: guard cell apoplast (osmotic) and guard cell symplast (hexokinase/ABA)

claims.why: It separates the two closure routes by compartment, so an apoplastic-osmotic result and a symplastic-signalling result need not be evidence for the same claim.

In summary, we posit that at low apoplastic sucrose concentra-

claims.section: Results, tests of the hexokinase hypothesis
claims.verbatim_text:
Previous reports in the literature42 have suggested a role for 
hexokinase as a guard-cell sugar sensor. However, neither treatment 
with N-acetyl-glucosamine (NAG), a pharmacological inhibitor of 
hexokinase43, nor genetic overexpression of hexokinase42 impacted 
sucrose enhancement of the guard-cell red-light response (Fig. 4e,f), 
ruling out a role for hexokinase.
claims.claim_statement: Neither pharmacological inhibition of hexokinase nor hexokinase overexpression affected sucrose enhancement of the guard-cell red-light response, ruling out hexokinase in that effect.
claims.subject: hexokinase
claims.object: sucrose enhancement of the guard-cell red-light response

scope.conditions: red light; sucrose applied at 1 and 100 mM per the same figure

claims.why: It dissociates the sugar-opening pathway from hexokinase, so the opening and closing literatures can coexist through different sensors rather than being a direct contradiction.

notes:
SCOPE OF THIS FILE. Only link C1 was extracted, from the 14 assigned papers. All 40 spans were located with the run's quote_locator.py offset semantics and every span was re-read from disk and byte-compared before writing; no span is hand-counted and no quote is paraphrased inside verbatim_text.

THE CORPUS CONTAINS BOTH DIRECTIONS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME EXPERIMENT. The two literatures differ systematically along four axes, and those differences are the reconciliation:
(1) COMPARTMENT. Closure evidence is either apoplastic-osmotic (sucrose accumulating in the guard cell wall of a transpiring leaf: A1-009, A1-012, A1-014) or symplastic-signalling (hexose phosphorylated by hexokinase inside the guard cell, triggering ABA: A1-002, A1-005, A1-008). 538 (A1-007) states these as two explicitly separate mechanisms. Opening evidence is about the guard cell CYTOSOLIC pool sourced from starch (A1-027, A1-028, A1-036) or imported through STP1/STP4 (A1-033, A1-034, A1-035).
(2) CONCENTRATION. This is the strongest single reconciler. 432 (A1-001) reports that hexoses and sucrose have little or no effect at low concentrations and close stomata at higher ones; 236 (A1-015, A1-021) reports the mirror image from the other side, enhancement at 0.4-1 mM and loss of enhancement at 30-100 mM. Two reviews independently converge on concentration-dependent sign flip (A1-018, A1-019). Caution: in 236 the 100 mM inhibition is reproduced by mannitol (A1-014), so the high-concentration arm is at least partly an osmotic artefact of the treatment, not sugar signalling.
(3) TIMESCALE / TIME OF DAY. Opening evidence is concentrated at dawn and in the first 30-60 min of light (A1-027, A1-028, A1-029, A1-033, A1-035, A1-036). Closure evidence is concentrated at midday and afternoon under carbon saturation (A1-006, A1-011, A1-012, A1-019, A1-039). 665 (A1-006) explicitly states the sucrose-hexokinase route can only provide LONG-term coordination and cannot account for short-term coordination. This is directly load-bearing: the hypothesis asserts a next-morning effect from one cold night, which sits in the short-term window that 665 says this mechanism does not cover.
(4) SENSOR PATHWAY. 236 (A1-025) actively rules hexokinase out of the sugar-enhancement-of-opening effect using both a pharmacological inhibitor and overexpression. So the opening route and the hexokinase closing route are dissociable, and the two literatures need not be in direct conflict.

WHAT THE ASSIGNED PAPERS DO NOT SHOW. I found no span in these 14 papers that measures dawn or early-morning leaf hexose against same-morning stomatal conductance, which is the specific test C4 requires. I also found no span linking night temperature to guard cell sugar status. Absence here is absence in my assigned set only, not evidence of absence in the 1,281-paper corpus.

PAPERS THAT YIELDED NOTHING FOR C1. 034_CO2_responsiveness_of_plants_a_possible_link_to_phloem_loadi contains no occurrence of 'stomat' or 'conductance' anywhere in its text; it is about leaf TNC and phloem-loading type under elevated CO2 and carries zero C1 evidence (it may serve C2/C3). 663_Resolving_the_central_metabolism_of_Arabidopsis_guard_cells is a flux-balance/13C study of guard cell central metabolism (it predicts a sucrose futile cycle and PEPc-derived malate) but makes no directional claim about sugar and aperture, so I extracted no claim from it rather than manufacturing one.

CLAIMS I DROPPED FOR LACK OF VERIFIABILITY. None were dropped for failed span verification; every candidate I kept re-extracted byte-identically. Four candidate quotes were rejected earlier in drafting because the extracted PDF text broke them across a column or box boundary so that a contiguous span would have spliced unrelated sentences (notably the 1106 sentence ending 'whereas the same sugars initiate stomatal closure later', which is separated from its continuation 'during the day when plants are carbon-saturated' by the whole of Box 2 in the extracted text). I did not quote across those breaks.
